material_systems.name: 100% Acrylic Latex Exterior Primer for Wood Windows

products: Benjamin Moore Ultra Spec EXT Primer
PPG Sun Proof Exterior Latex Primer
primer.notes: Standard exterior acrylic primer for bare wood window frames, sashes, and muntins. Penetrates wood grain, remains flexible long-term. For tannin-rich species (cedar, redwood, fir), supplement with alkyd spot-prime at knots BEFORE this full coat. Seal all end-grain on sash edges (top/bottom rails) with extra primer pass. Per Exterior_Primer_Systems_Doctrine.md section 4: 400-450 SF/gal on smooth surfaces.

material_systems.notes: Primary primer for bare wood windows on new construction. Factory-primed wood windows in good condition (SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY) may skip field prime. End-grain sealing on sash rail edges is critical moisture protection.

material_systems.name: Alkyd/Shellac Spot Primer for Tannin Knots on Wood Windows

primer.type: Stain-blocking alkyd or shellac-based spot primer
products: KILZ Original Multi-Surface Stain Blocking Primer
primer.notes: Spot-applied to visible knots on tannin-rich species (cedar, redwood, Douglas fir) BEFORE full acrylic primer coat. Not a full-surface system -- applied per knot/stain location by brush. Alkyd has superior tannin stain blocking vs acrylic. Shellac-based (BIN) for extreme cases. Per Exterior_Primer_Systems_Doctrine.md section 2.

material_systems.notes: Conditional on wood species -- required for tannin-rich species (cedar, redwood, fir). Applied by brush to individual knots before full acrylic primer coat. Quantity is per-knot, not SF-based.

material_systems.name: Corrosion-Inhibiting Primer for Aluminum-Clad Windows

products: Sherwin-Williams Pro Industrial DTM Acrylic Primer
primer.notes: MANDATORY for aluminum-clad windows even over factory finish. Aluminum is nonporous, slick substrate -- requires mechanical bonding profile (180-220 grit scuff-sand) BEFORE primer application. Corrosion-inhibiting formula prevents oxidation under paint film. Per Exterior_Windows_Painting_Doctrine.md section 4.

material_systems.notes: Field prime is MANDATORY for aluminum-clad even when factory finish exists. Factory finish on aluminum is cosmetic only -- does not provide adequate bonding profile for architectural-grade topcoat. SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD skips this system.

material_systems.name: PVC Bonding Primer for Vinyl-Clad Windows

products: Benjamin Moore Insl-X Stix Bonding Primer
primer.notes: MANDATORY for vinyl-clad windows. Grips dense, non-porous PVC surface while providing mechanical tooth for topcoat. CAUTION: bonding primer left exposed too long dries like 'peanut brittle' -- loses flexibility for topcoat bond. Recoat within 1 week per Exterior_Primer_Systems_Doctrine.md section 5. Clean vinyl with TSP substitute before application (no sanding required).

material_systems.notes: Field prime is MANDATORY for vinyl-clad even when factory finish exists. Standard primers will NOT adhere to vinyl. SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD skips this system.

material_systems.name: Standard Exterior Acrylic Window Paint

products: PPG Sun Proof Exterior Acrylic Latex
finish.notes: Mid-grade 100% acrylic exterior trim enamel for QT3 window painting. Hard enamel for UV resistance, flexible for thermal expansion cycles. Two coats standard on primed surfaces. Glass lap 1/16 inch overlap onto glass is MANDATORY -- encapsulates putty/sealant, creates weather-tight seal. Sheen is project-level selection (satin, semi-gloss, or gloss) -- no locked-in default.

material_systems.notes: Standard exterior window finish for QT3. Coverage rate reflects small surface area with high cut-in ratio -- brush application on narrow frame and sash profiles reduces effective coverage vs field siding.

material_systems.name: Premium Exterior Urethane-Modified Acrylic Window Paint

finish.notes: Premium acrylic-urethane with enhanced hardness, gloss retention, and UV resistance. Self-leveling for brush-mark-free finish on detailed muntin work. QT4: light sand 220-grit between coats, raking light inspection. QT5: hand-sand 220-320 grit between coats, raking light at multiple angles, DFT verification. Sheen is project-level selection -- no locked-in default.

material_systems.notes: Premium/superior exterior window finish for QT4 and QT5. Higher solids content yields slightly lower coverage per gallon. Self-leveling property is critical for TDL muntin bars where brush marks are highly visible.

material_systems.name: VinylSafe IR-Reflective Exterior Enamel for Vinyl-Clad Windows

finish.type: IR-Reflective Acrylic with Complex Inorganic Color Pigments (CICPs)
products: Benjamin Moore Colors for Vinyl (select palette)
finish.notes: MANDATORY for vinyl-clad windows when color LRV < 55. CICPs absorb visible light for dark visual appearance while reflecting near-infrared radiation, dropping surface temperature 20-30 deg F. Without VinylSafe: standard dark paint causes warping, seal failure, and voids manufacturer warranty. HARD STOP -- do not apply standard paint with LRV < 55 to vinyl-clad windows. Per Exterior_Color_Sheen_Configuration_Doctrine.md sections 1-2.

material_systems.notes: Conditional system -- replaces standard or premium finish when cladding = vinyl_clad AND color LRV < 55. Applies across all quality tiers. Slightly lower coverage due to specialty CICP pigment formulation. Color palette is more limited than standard paint lines.

small.notes: Small window (glass area < 6 SF): ~3-5 SF paintable frame/sash surface per EA.

medium.notes: Medium window (glass area 6-15 SF): ~5-10 SF paintable surface per EA. Calibration baseline.

large.notes: Large window (glass area > 15 SF): ~10-20 SF paintable surface per EA. Bay/bow at upper end.

ea_conversion.notes: Paintable surface is frame + sash + muntins (if TDL/SDL). Excludes glass area. Window size bucket determines SF-per-EA conversion for material quantity.

SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD.notes: New wood window -- smooth mill finish. Moderate absorption at end grain (sash rail edges). Coverage per Exterior_Primer_Systems_Doctrine.md section 4.

coverage_profiles.waste_notes: 15% waste factor for window painting. Higher than door (10%) due to small, detailed surfaces with greater brush loading waste. Consistent with exterior trim waste factor.
assumptions: Coverage rates per Exterior_Primer_Systems_Doctrine.md section 4 (400-450 SF/gal smooth).
SF-per-window estimates derived from standard window sizing. Actual varies by manufacturer.
TDL muntins add ~10-20% to paintable SF per window (muntin bar faces and edges).
Spray application: multiply material quantity by 1.25-1.33 for transfer efficiency loss on small surfaces.

ea_conversion.notes: Same SF-per-EA as wood profile. Aluminum-clad window frame geometry is similar.

SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY.notes: Corrosion-inhibiting primer over scuff-sanded aluminum factory finish. Non-porous substrate -- consistent coverage. Slightly lower than acrylic on wood due to higher film build.

coverage_profiles.waste_notes: 15% waste factor consistent with exterior trim/window standards.
assumptions: Coverage based on smooth aluminum-clad surface -- non-porous, predictable.
Scuff-sanding creates bonding profile but does not increase porosity significantly.

ea_conversion.notes: Same SF-per-EA as other profiles. Vinyl-clad window frame geometry is similar.

SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY.notes: PVC bonding primer on vinyl-clad surface. Non-porous substrate -- consistent coverage. Good primer build.

coverage_profiles.waste_notes: 15% waste factor consistent with exterior trim/window standards.
assumptions: PVC/vinyl surface is consistently smooth and non-porous -- predictable coverage.
Bonding primer must be recoated within 1 week to avoid brittleness.

ea_conversion.notes: Finish coverage on primed (sealed) surface -- more consistent than primer coverage regardless of original substrate.

SYS_EXT_WIN_FINISH_STANDARD.notes: Standard acrylic on primed window. Consistent, predictable coverage on sealed surface.

SYS_EXT_WIN_FINISH_PREMIUM.notes: Premium acrylic-urethane has higher solids -- slightly lower coverage per gallon. Better film build per coat.

SYS_EXT_WIN_FINISH_VINYLSAFE.notes: IR-reflective formulation with CICP pigments -- reduced coverage compared to standard acrylic. Specialty pigment formulation.

coverage_profiles.waste_notes: 15% waste factor for window finish coats. Two coats standard at all quality tiers.
assumptions: Coverage is per coat -- multiply by 2 for total material per window.
Spray application: multiply material by 1.25-1.33 for transfer efficiency on small surfaces.
TDL muntin bars add ~10-20% additional paintable surface per window.
Glass lap (1/16 inch) has negligible material impact.

consumables.name: Angled Sash Brush 2 inch
consumables.notes: PRIMARY applicator for exterior window painting. 2-inch angular sash brush is the workhorse -- precision control for 1/16 inch glass lap, sash stile/rail painting, and cutting in around glass. Per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine.md: 1 brush per material type. ~5,000 LF lifespan with care. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Angled Sash Brush 1.5 inch
consumables.notes: Detail brush for TDL/SDL muntin bar painting. Narrow muntin bars (3/4 to 1 inch wide) require smaller brush for clean lines. Also used for glazing putty painting. Only needed when muntin_type = tdl or sdl. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Airless Spray Tip 211 (window precision)
consumables.notes: 211 tip (0.011 inch orifice, 4-inch fan) for precision on small window frame surfaces. Tight fan pattern essential for window components. Used only when application_method = spray (whole-house spray context). Per Exterior_Application_Methods_Doctrine.md.

consumables.name: 200-Mesh Spray Filter (red) for Window Precision
consumables.notes: Fine 200-mesh (red) filter for window spray applications. Finer filtration than standard 60-mesh to prevent tip clogging on small orifice tips. Only applicable when application_method = spray.

consumables.name: Extension Pole (4-8 ft)
consumables.notes: For upper window reach from ground level or scaffold. Reduces ladder repositioning on single-story windows. Reusable across project.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 180 Grit
consumables.notes: Scuff-sand aluminum-clad window surfaces (180-220 grit range) to create mechanical bonding profile before corrosion-inhibiting primer. Per Exterior_Windows_Painting_Doctrine.md section 4. Also used for initial prep sanding on wood windows. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220 Grit
consumables.notes: Intercoat sanding between finish coats. QT3: visual inspect only -- no intercoat sand. QT4: light scuff sand 220-grit between finish coats with raking light inspection. QT5: hand-sand 220-grit (first pass). Also used for aluminum-clad scuff-sanding. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 320 Grit
consumables.notes: Fine sanding for QT5 intercoat work. Second pass after 220-grit for showroom-quality smoothness. Required on all visible surfaces including muntin bars. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Tack Cloth
consumables.notes: Dust removal after sanding before prime or finish coat. Required after all sanding operations. Small window surfaces mean higher window count per tack cloth vs doors. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: TSP Substitute Cleaner
consumables.notes: For aluminum-clad (remove oxidation/chalking) and vinyl-clad (general clean) prep. Non-phosphate formula per environmental regulations. Also used for general window cleaning before painting on all cladding types.

consumables.name: Sash Lubricant (light wax or linseed oil)
consumables.notes: Applied to unpainted sliding channels (pulley stiles) and other contact points on operable windows. Prevents sash binding after paint cure. NEVER paint these surfaces -- lubricate only. Per Exterior_Windows_Painting_Doctrine.md section 3. Only applicable to operable windows (not fixed).

consumables.name: Exterior Wood Filler
consumables.notes: For filling small defects, nail holes, and minor damage on wood window frames and sashes. Exterior-rated filler that remains flexible. For extensive sill rot or sash rot: two-part structural epoxy (separate scope). Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Glazing Putty (Sarco Dual Glaze)
consumables.notes: CONDITIONAL -- only for wood windows with traditional glazing compound. Sarco Dual Glaze recommended for field use. Avoid big-box putties (dry inconsistently, mildew easily). Requires curing/skinning time before painting. Per Exterior_Windows_Painting_Doctrine.md section 1.

consumables.name: Painter's Tape (exterior grade)
consumables.notes: UV-resistant exterior masking tape. 14-day removal rating minimum. Used for glass masking edge seal, sill protection tape, casing-edge protection, and general edge masking. Per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine.md: all tape rolls yield 180 LF (60 yards). Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Fine Line Masking Tape (1/8 inch or 1/4 inch)
consumables.notes: Precision tape for glass lap line. Creates the 1/16 inch paint-to-glass overlap that forms the weather seal. Score with utility knife before removal for razor-sharp paint line. Critical for QT4/QT5 window finish quality.

consumables.name: HDPE Static-Cling Glass Masking Film
consumables.notes: Static-cling HDPE film for glass pane masking on standard single-lite windows. Faster application than tape-and-paper. Requires secondary tape line to prevent film flutter from wind during exterior work. SAFE for Low-E glass -- no scoring required for removal.

consumables.name: Masking Paper for Glass Panes
consumables.notes: Alternative to HDPE film for glass masking. Brown kraft masking paper applied with tape at glass edges. Used when HDPE film is not available or when wind conditions make static-cling unreliable. Also used for TDL windows where individual panes are small.

consumables.name: Liquid Glass Masking Product (Jasco Mask & Peel)
consumables.notes: Brush-on liquid mask for TDL (true divided lite) muntin windows. Cures into protective membrane over each individual glass pane. Score trim line and peel post-painting. Dramatically faster than tape-and-film on multi-lite TDL windows. PROHIBITED on Low-E glass -- scoring damages Low-E coating. Per Exterior_Windows_Painting_Doctrine.md section 8.

consumables.name: Hardware Storage Bags with Labels
consumables.notes: Labeled ziplock bags for storing removed window hardware -- locks, lifts, sash pulls. One bag per operable window. Label with window location and hardware contents. Fixed windows have no removable hardware. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Razor Blade / Utility Knife Blade
consumables.notes: For scoring masking tape at glass edge for clean removal. Also for cutting in stuck sashes and removing paint drips from glass. Replace blade when dull to avoid scratching glass. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: TSP or TSP-Substitute Detergent
consumables.notes: General cleaning on all cladding types before painting. Removes dirt, grime, oxidation, chalking. Critical for aluminum-clad prep per Exterior_Windows_Painting_Doctrine.md section 4. Reused consumable ID.

ext_window_glass_mask.description: Glass pane masking in window assembly during window painting
ext_window_glass_mask.notes: Glass masking is MANDATORY for all window painting -- brush or spray. Method selection: (1) Low-E glass = tape-and-film ONLY (liquid mask prohibited). (2) TDL + non-Low-E = liquid mask preferred (faster). (3) Single-lite = HDPE static-cling film + secondary tape line. Glass lap 1/16 inch overlap is intentional -- masking line must account for this. Masking time varies dramatically: single-lite 0.08-0.12 hrs/EA, TDL 0.20-0.50 hrs/EA.

ext_window_hardware.description: Window hardware removal, storage, and reinstallation
ext_window_hardware.notes: Hardware is REMOVED per doctrine -- not masked. Locks, lifts, sash pulls bagged and labeled per window. Fixed windows have no operable hardware. Applies to all operable types: awning, casement, double-hung. Reinstall after final coat is dry.

ext_window_weatherstrip.description: Weatherstrip protection -- remove friction-fit or deep-tape non-removable
ext_window_weatherstrip.notes: NEVER paint weatherstripping. Friction-fit stripping: gently pull out, re-insert after finish is dry. Non-removable stripping: deep-tape into gap with putty knife. Tape consumed only when stripping cannot be removed. Fixed windows have no weatherstripping. Per Exterior_Windows_Painting_Doctrine.md section 3.

ext_sill_protection.description: Exterior window sill protection from drips during window painting
ext_sill_protection.notes: Protect finished exterior sill from drips during window frame/sash painting. Tape and paper over sill surface. Only needed when sill is already finished (from trim spec). If sill is painted simultaneously, no protection needed.

ext_window_casing_adjacent.description: Protect finished casing from window painting drips
ext_window_casing_adjacent.notes: Light tape at casing-to-frame junction when casing is already finished. Minimal masking -- only at junction line. Only needed when casing was painted by trim spec before window spec. If painted together, coordinate sequence to avoid this protection.

ext_siding_adjacent.description: Protect finished siding adjacent to window during spray application
ext_siding_adjacent.notes: When spraying windows, siding adjacent to window must be masked to prevent overspray on finished or unfinished siding. Only applicable when application_method = spray. Brush application has minimal overspray -- no siding masking needed. No dedicated PaintScope key -- siding masking quantity is derived from window count being sprayed.

compatibility_rules.description: Acrylic primer for bare wood windows
compatibility_rules.notes: Standard 100% acrylic exterior primer for bare wood. Remains flexible, breathable. End-grain sealing on sash edges is critical.

compatibility_rules.description: Tannin spot-prime required for tannin-rich wood species
compatibility_rules.notes: Alkyd/shellac spot primer on visible knots before full acrylic primer coat. Prevents tannin bleed staining through finish. Per Exterior_Primer_Systems_Doctrine.md section 2.

compatibility_rules.description: Corrosion-inhibiting primer MANDATORY for aluminum-clad windows
compatibility_rules.notes: Aluminum is nonporous slick substrate. Standard acrylic primer will NOT adhere. Must scuff-sand 180-220 grit THEN apply corrosion-inhibiting primer. MANDATORY even over factory finish. Per Exterior_Windows_Painting_Doctrine.md section 4.

compatibility_rules.description: PVC bonding primer MANDATORY for vinyl-clad windows
compatibility_rules.notes: Vinyl is dense, non-porous, low-surface-energy substrate. Standard primers will NOT bond. Bonding primer mandatory. Must recoat within 1 week. Per Exterior_Windows_Painting_Doctrine.md section 4.

compatibility_rules.description: VinylSafe IR-reflective finish MANDATORY for vinyl-clad with dark colors (LRV < 55)
compatibility_rules.notes: HARD STOP -- standard dark paint on vinyl-clad windows causes warping, seal failure, voids warranty. VinylSafe IR-reflective coating is non-negotiable when vinyl + LRV < 55. Per Exterior_Color_Sheen_Configuration_Doctrine.md sections 1-2.

compatibility_rules.description: Liquid masking PROHIBITED on Low-E glass
compatibility_rules.notes: Scoring liquid mask to create trim line DAMAGES Low-E coating on glass. Tape-and-film method ONLY when Low-E glass is present. Per Exterior_Windows_Painting_Doctrine.md section 8. Most NC windows have Low-E glass.

compatibility_rules.description: Factory-primed wood may skip field prime
compatibility_rules.notes: Factory-primed wood windows in good condition may skip field prime and go direct to finish coats. Light degloss/scuff of factory primer before topcoat still required. This DIFFERS from aluminum/vinyl clad where field prime is mandatory even over factory finish.

compatibility_rules.description: Field-primed surfaces skip prime module entirely
compatibility_rules.notes: Direct topcoat application on field-primed surfaces regardless of cladding type. Skip prime module entirely.

compatibility_rules.description: Never paint sliding channels, weatherstripping, or sash cords
compatibility_rules.notes: Per Exterior_Windows_Painting_Doctrine.md section 3: NEVER paint pulley stiles (sliding channels), weatherstripping, or sash cords. Lubricate with light wax or linseed oil. Painting these causes sash binding, weatherstrip brittleness, cord failure.

compatibility_rules.description: Bonding primer recoat window -- 1 week maximum
compatibility_rules.notes: Bonding primer on vinyl-clad windows must be topcoated within 1 week. Beyond that, primer loses flexibility (dries like 'peanut brittle') and topcoat bond is compromised. If exceeded: scuff-sand before topcoat. Per Exterior_Primer_Systems_Doctrine.md section 5.

risk_notes.topic: Vinyl-clad thermal distortion from dark standard paint
risk_notes.risk: Standard dark paint (LRV < 55) on vinyl-clad windows causes excessive heat absorption, leading to warping, seal failure, and voided manufacturer warranty.
risk_notes.mitigation: Use VinylSafe IR-reflective coating (SYS_EXT_WIN_FINISH_VINYLSAFE) on ALL vinyl-clad windows with color LRV < 55. HARD STOP -- no exceptions.

risk_notes.topic: Low-E glass damage from liquid masking
risk_notes.risk: Scoring liquid masking product on Low-E coated glass damages the specialized Low-E coating, destroying its thermal performance permanently.
risk_notes.mitigation: PROHIBITED: liquid masking on Low-E glass. Tape-and-film method only. Most NC windows have Low-E glass. Per Exterior_Windows_Painting_Doctrine.md section 8.

risk_notes.topic: Sash blocking from improper drying procedure
risk_notes.risk: Paint acts as adhesive, sealing operable sashes shut ('blocking'). Especially problematic on double-hung windows where upper and lower sash can bond to frame.
risk_notes.mitigation: Follow sash drying protocol: leave 1 inch gap top and bottom until dry, periodically move sashes during drying. Never close sash fully until paint is completely cured. Per Exterior_Windows_Painting_Doctrine.md section 3.

risk_notes.topic: Adhesion failure on aluminum-clad without proper prep
risk_notes.risk: Aluminum factory finish is nonporous and slick. Paint applied without mechanical bonding profile (scuff-sanding) and corrosion-inhibiting primer peels in sheets.
risk_notes.mitigation: MANDATORY: scuff-sand 180-220 grit THEN apply SYS_EXT_WIN_PRIMER_CORROSION. Skip = guaranteed adhesion failure.

risk_notes.risk: PVC bonding primer left exposed beyond 1 week dries like 'peanut brittle' -- loses flexibility needed for topcoat adhesion bond on vinyl-clad windows.
risk_notes.mitigation: Apply topcoat within 1 week of bonding primer application. If exceeded, scuff-sand before topcoat. Per Exterior_Primer_Systems_Doctrine.md section 5.

risk_notes.topic: Moisture infiltration from missing glass lap
risk_notes.risk: Without 1/16 inch paint overlap onto glass, glazing compound/sealant is exposed to UV and moisture. Failed glazing allows rain to pool in wood rebate, causing rot and peeling around glass perimeter.
risk_notes.mitigation: Glass lap 1/16 inch overlap is MANDATORY -- not a defect, it is the weather seal. Verify at final inspection. Per Exterior_Windows_Painting_Doctrine.md section 3.

risk_notes.topic: Tannin bleed through finish on wood windows
risk_notes.risk: Cedar, redwood, and fir window frames bleed tannins through standard acrylic primer, causing brown/yellow staining on finish coat.
risk_notes.mitigation: Spot-prime visible knots with alkyd or shellac-based primer (SYS_EXT_WIN_PRIMER_TANNIN_SPOT) before full acrylic primer coat.

risk_notes.topic: Temperature blisters from painting in direct sunlight
risk_notes.risk: Direct sunlight heats fresh paint on window surfaces. Surface skins prematurely while trapped solvents expand into blisters underneath.
risk_notes.mitigation: 'Follow the sun' -- paint window in shade. Schedule painting sequence by elevation based on sun tracking. Per Exterior_Windows_Painting_Doctrine.md section 7.

risk_notes.risk: Paint on weatherstripping destroys elasticity, causes brittleness and seal tearing. Results in air/water infiltration at window perimeter.
risk_notes.mitigation: Remove friction-fit stripping before painting. Deep-tape non-removable stripping. NEVER paint over weatherstrip material. Per Exterior_Windows_Painting_Doctrine.md section 3.

material_quantity_notes.ea_based_system: This spec uses EA (each) as the primary UOM. Material quantities are calculated per window assembly by size bucket. Each window assembly includes exterior frame, sash(es), and muntins (if TDL/SDL). Excludes glass area, interior surfaces, and casing (trim spec scope).

sf_per_window_by_size.small: 3-5 SF paintable surface per EA (glass area < 6 SF). Awning, casement, fixed.
sf_per_window_by_size.medium: 5-10 SF paintable surface per EA (glass area 6-15 SF). Calibration baseline.
sf_per_window_by_size.large: 10-20 SF paintable surface per EA (glass area > 15 SF). Bay/bow at upper end.

material_quantity_notes.muntin_sf_impact: TDL (true divided lite) muntins add ~10-20% additional paintable surface per window. SDL (simulated divided lite) adds ~5-10% (applied bars only). GBG/none = no additional surface.
material_quantity_notes.waste_factor: 15% material waste for window painting -- small detailed surfaces with high brush loading waste. Consistent with exterior trim waste factor (15%). Higher than doors (10%) due to more complex geometry.
material_quantity_notes.spray_transfer_efficiency: Airless spray on windows: 60-70% transfer efficiency. Lower than doors (75-80%) due to smaller target surfaces with higher edge-to-surface ratio. Multiply theoretical coverage by 1.30-1.40.
material_quantity_notes.two_coat_standard: Standard coat system: 1 prime + 2 finish coats on bare/factory-primed substrates. SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD: 2 finish coats only (skip prime). Aluminum/vinyl clad with SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY: still require field prime (1 prime + 2 finish).
material_quantity_notes.glass_masking_material_note: Glass masking material consumption varies dramatically by muntin_type. Single-lite: ~2 LF tape + 1 SF film per pane. TDL 6-lite: ~12 LF tape + 6 SF film (or 0.5 oz liquid mask). TDL 12-lite: ~24 LF tape + 12 SF film (or 1 oz liquid mask).

assumptions.value: Small: 3-5 SF, Medium: 5-10 SF, Large: 10-20 SF paintable surface per window assembly
assumptions.source: User brief; standard window sizing; resolution.json paintable_items
assumptions.note: Doctrine provides hours/coat rates by window type but does not specify SF per window. SF estimates derived from standard window dimensions. Used for material quantity conversion only.

assumptions.value: 350-400 SF/gal for corrosion-inhibiting primer on aluminum-clad
assumptions.note: No doctrine-specific coverage for corrosion-inhibiting primer on aluminum-clad windows. Derived from sibling door spec DTM primer coverage on smooth metal.

assumptions.value: 350-400 SF/gal for PVC bonding primer on vinyl-clad
assumptions.note: Matches sibling trim spec bonding primer coverage on PVC substrate.
No doctrine-specific coverage for VinylSafe paint on windows. Derived from sibling trim and door spec IR-reflective coverage. CICP pigment formulation reduces coverage vs standard acrylic.
Using 15% consistent with exterior trim. Higher than doors (10%) because window components are smaller and more detailed, leading to greater brush loading waste.

assumptions.value: Field prime mandatory for aluminum-clad even over factory finish
assumptions.note: Doctrine explicitly requires corrosion-inhibiting primer for aluminum-clad. Factory finish is cosmetic only.

assumptions.value: Field prime mandatory for vinyl-clad even over factory finish
assumptions.note: Doctrine explicitly requires PVC bonding primer for vinyl-clad. Standard primers will not bond to vinyl.

uncertainty_flags.description: SF-per-window estimates by size bucket (S/M/L) are extrapolated from standard window dimensions. Actual paintable surface varies significantly by manufacturer, window type, and muntin configuration.
uncertainty_flags.action: Validate against field measurements of actual windows by size bucket. Consider manufacturer-specific SF data for common window brands.

uncertainty_flags.description: Liquid mask usage rate (1 QT per 6-8 TDL windows) is estimated from product data. Actual varies by lite count, glass pane size, and application thickness.
uncertainty_flags.action: Validate against field usage data for Jasco Mask & Peel on TDL windows.

uncertainty_flags.description: HDPE static-cling film usage rate (1 ROLL per 15-20 windows) is estimated. Roll sizes vary by manufacturer. Secondary tape line adds tape consumption.
uncertainty_flags.action: Validate against field practice. Quantify secondary tape usage for wind flutter prevention.

uncertainty_flags.description: Resolution indicates factory-primed wood windows may skip field prime. No explicit adhesion test protocol defined for this decision gate.
uncertainty_flags.action: Flag for field calibration. Consider adding adhesion test protocol (ASTM D3359 cross-hatch tape pull) as explicit decision gate.
